confirmed.claim: The exactly-once ledger (outputs/remote_consumed.json) is capped at CONSUMED_CAP=500 entries (_save_consumed trims to entries[-CONSUMED_CAP:]), but a consumed command's queue file on the branch is deleted only when push_pc_status() next runs successfully (its deletes list is built from the CURRENT, already-trimmed consumed list). If push_pc_status is disabled (LB_NO_STATUS_PUSH), keeps failing, or simply hasn't run yet, and >=500 further commands accumulate in the ledger in the meantime, an already-applied command's id falls off the trimmed ledger while its queue file is still present on the branch -- so the next poll_once() sees it as 'fresh' again and re-forwards it to the runner, violating the module's own documented invariant ('EXACTLY-ONCE: ... a command id is forwarded at most once, ever').
confirmed.evidence: _save_consumed (line 234): tmp.write_text(json.dumps(entries[-CONSUMED_CAP:], ...)). poll_once's dedup at line 368: seen = {e.get('id') for e in consumed} -- an id trimmed out of consumed is no longer in seen. push_pc_status's delete computation (lines 440, 492-493): consumed = _load_consumed(root) then deletes built only from currently-retained ids.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Status push disabled or persistently failing (e.g. offline PC, or LB_NO_STATUS_PUSH=1 set for a stretch) while the operator issues 500+ remote commands (or the same handful retried enough times to accumulate 500 ledger entries) after a flatten_all/pause/etc. was applied and ledgered; once status push resumes and the old entry has already fallen off the ledger tail, poll_once re-forwards the same flatten_all command to the runner a second time, which -- unlike a replay-protected exit action -- can flatten positions the operator never asked about a second time (the exact C-F5 scenario this file's own comments say the ledger exists to prevent).

verdict.reason: Mechanism verified at scripts/remote_control.py:234 (trim), :368 (seen built from retained ledger only), :492-493 (deletes built from retained ledger only); no runner-side id dedup and no test pins the cap. However the claim omits that validate_command re-checks MAX_AGE_SEC=1800 with fresh now on every re-encounter (line 204), so an id resurrected after trim is REJECTED as stale unless the 500 appends happened within 30 minutes of issued_at. Actual re-forward therefore requires push_pc_status dead AND either a ~500-command flood from a repo-write-access actor (already fully trusted per the module's own security model) or >~530 stale undeleted queue files accumulated over months of failed pushes. Outside that window the only symptom is ledger churn (re-reject/re-append noise). Invariant break is real and uncovered elsewhere, but severity WARNING is inflated by the unaccounted 30-min bound and the whitelist-limited blast radius (worst dup: flatten_all within 30 min). Downgrade to NOTE, SAFE_NOW (fix is ledger/GC bookkeeping, not order logic). Caught by SABOTEUR and SECURITY AUDITOR lenses independently, so NOTE ships.

confirmed.claim: The duplicate-fill-signature key is built by string-concatenating (purpose, side, rkey(size), rkey(price)) with raw control bytes 0x1F/0x1E as field/record separators, whereas the pre-registered Python reference (scripts/cohort_eval.py:299-300, 305) uses an actual tuple `(purpose, side, round(sz,6), round(px,4))` as the dict key. If a fills.csv row's `purpose` or `side` text cell itself contains byte 0x1E or 0x1F (a corrupted/torn write, or any adversarially crafted CSV cell -- both are within the file's own stated threat model of 'strict-ingest law: every malformed row is COUNTED, never coerced'), two distinct Python-side signature tuples can collide into the same C++ string, or vice versa. The C++ diode would then dedupe (or fail to dedupe) a trip differently than scripts/cohort_eval.era4_trips, silently diverging accrual_n / gross_pct / net_pct from the Python reference the header (lines 7-11) explicitly claims to mirror 'rule-for-rule' with '1e-9' differential agreement.
confirmed.evidence: diode/lb_diode.cpp lines 544-547 build `sig += purpose; sig += '\x1f'; sig += side...; sig += rkey(*sz,1e6); sig += '\x1f'; sig += rkey(*px,1e4); sig += '\x1e';` versus scripts/cohort_eval.py:299-300 `sig.append((r.get('purpose'), r.get('side'), round(sz,6), round(px,4)))` / `key = tuple(sig)`. No test in tests/test_cpp_diode.py exercises a purpose/side value containing 0x1E or 0x1F (grepped, no hits) -- the collision path is untested and undocumented anywhere in the file's own commentary, unlike the other known, called-out approximations (nan-ts sort key, banker's-vs-away-from-zero rounding) which the code explicitly reasons about and dismisses.

verdict.reason: Mechanism confirmed: C++ CSV reader (lb_diode.cpp:151) and Python csv both pass 0x1F/0x1E through as ordinary cell bytes, rkey outputs never contain them, so purpose/side are real injection channels and a crafted pair (e.g. purpose="entry\x1fsell",side="X" vs purpose="entry",side="sell\x1fX", equal sz/px) collides in the C++ string key while staying distinct Python tuples — C++ drops a trip Python keeps, diverging accrual_n. Corrupt legs bypass the esz/xsz/opened_by filters when the trip also has genuine entry+exit legs. However the offered severity is inflated and half the threat model is refuted: a corrupted/torn write CANNOT trigger it — a lone random control byte yields a key unique in both representations (identical dedup outcome); only a deliberately crafted colliding pair diverges, and an actor able to craft outputs/fills.csv already owns the ground truth and can forge accrual numbers directly. The diode is DIODE-LAW offline/report-only, never in a decision path, so worst case is a wrong referee report on an attacker-controlled file. It survives as NOTE because the file's own contract ("rule-for-rule", 1e-9, documents every other divergence corner: underscores 69-70, banker's rounding 451-456, nan-ts 489-493) makes an undocumented non-injectivity corner a defect by the codebase's own standard, untested in test_cpp_diode.py, and two lenses independently catch it (security auditor: crafted cell across trust boundary; new hire: header's mirror claim conceals an unwritten exception). Fix = document the corner or escape separators in the sig builder; SAFE_NOW classification correct.
